contributions.title: Twelve added lines and one removed line in two program files off base dc11c774: three assertions and a comment at the entry of one handler, one crate import widened, and one appended error enum. That is the whole of this candidate. The problem it names is a create funding a vault that no state descr

alternatives: Alternative: make no code change and rely only on the Create account constraints, which at base already bind the vault's mint to mint_a, its authority to the new state, and its existence to a fresh init; because the handler guards read the same three properties from the same accounts, they may add no rejection the constraints do not already produce.

Alternative: express the same invariants as explicit anchor constraint expressions on the Create struct instead of handler requires, so rejection happens at account resolution before any CPI and before rent is committed, and no new error enum is needed.

Alternative: answer the question this change implies with fixture cases rather than with a guard - a second create for the same maker and escrow_id, and a create whose derived vault address already exists in the associated token program.
Alternative: rely on the built-in constraint errors and drop the state/mod.rs enum, since ConstraintTokenMint and ConstraintTokenOwner already exist for two of the three conditions.
narrative.integration: The change is additive and self-contained: one enum appended in state/mod.rs and four lines at the entry of one handler, with the Create and Take account structs, the instruction signatures, the seeds and the GifterEscrow layout untouched, so escrows already created keep their addresses, their vaults and their settlement path, and no migration or reallocation is implied. Integrate it as hardening behind constraints that already exclude the same conditions at base, describe it in those words rather than as a vulnerability fix, and pair it with the two fixture cases that would exercise the guards - a create whose vault is not the state's associated token account and a create whose vault already holds tokens - because without them the only observable effect is a new error name. Any client that maps program errors may need a branch for the new variant; the numeric code is an authoritative field for code assembly and is not stated in this narrative.
limitations: Narrative drafted by the Sol.College CTO agent; authoritative fields (commits, evidence, hashes) are assembled by code.
narrative.problem: Twelve added lines and one removed line in two program files off base dc11c774: three assertions and a comment at the entry of one handler, one crate import widened, and one appended error enum. That is the whole of this candidate. The problem it names is a create funding a vault that no state describes. The honest scope is narrower than that phrasing: at base dc11c774 the Create accounts struct already binds escrow_vault to the new state's associated token account for mint_a and requires a fresh init, so the three conditions the handler now checks are the ones the account constraints already exclude before the handler runs. What the candidate adds is a program-defined rejection path with a named error inside the program - defence in depth, a clearer error surface, and intent recorded in code - not the closure of an input the base admitted. Adoption should therefore be described as hardening, and it should travel with the fixture cases that exercise it. Validation status is taken only from the evidence id, and no acceptance is claimed here.
risks: The problem statement rests on a create funding a vault that no state describes, but at base dc11c774 the accounts struct appears to exclude exactly that before the handler runs, so the records supplied do not establish that an observed violation occurred; if the intent was to close an observed exposure, the evidence for it is not in this envelope and should be named before adoption.

The mint guard's redundancy depends on initialize_gifter_escrow running before deposit_to_escrow_vault, which holds at base; a change to that call order would make the guard load-bearing, and nothing in this diff asserts or tests the order.

The numeric error code assigned to VaultNotEmpty, and any client mapping of it, are authoritative fields owned by code assembly; they are not established by the records read for this narrative and are deliberately not stated.

The evidence establishes a successful build and a successful local-validator fixture step on this candidate SHA; I did not read the fixture's case list, its assertions or the job logs, so which cases ran, and whether either new guard was exercised, is not established. Coverage is a local validator only: no devnet, no mainnet, no upgrade path and no client behaviour.

The fixture runs inside the untrusted job and the verdict is recorded by a separate attest job that checks out no candidate code; that separation is what makes the record credible, and it adds no coverage.
The candidate commit is unsigned, with verification.verified false and reason unsigned, and authored by automation, so provenance rests on the PR body and the run record rather than on a signature.

The envelope's research source asks about take_and_close and the PDA signer seeds, which is the settlement path, while this candidate touches the create path only; the relationship between the candidate and that research question is not established by the supplied records.

Because escrow_vault uses init, a derived vault address that already exists makes the create fail at account resolution before the new guards run, so the guards change nothing in that case; any residual exposure there, such as rent locked in an account the maker cannot use, is outside this diff and outside what these records measure.
narrative.rollback: The candidate is a single commit whose parent is the base dc11c774, so rollback is a revert of that one commit against the same base and returns the tree to base exactly, with no state migration, no account reallocation and no seed change implied; escrows created while the change was live stay readable and settleable because neither the state layout nor the vault derivation depends on it. What a rollback gives up is the program-defined error name and the comment that records intent; on the reading above that name is likely unreachable in the create path, so the practical loss is documentation rather than behaviour. The branch is a lab branch with merged_at null, so not advancing it is itself a rollback and needs no revert commit.
